bioAdditions:
Frederick Aloysius Meier registered for the WWI draft in June 1917 at 298 Barney Street, Wilkes-Barre, his parents' address. He gave his birth as 15 Sep 1892 at Hazleton and was a moulder in the Vulcan Iron Works, Wilkes-Barre, with a wife and one child under 12 to support (S1). He married Anna Mather on 21 Apr 1915 (FS tree). Their children, per the FamilySearch tree, were Florence Irene (1916–1933), Fred A. Jr. (1918–2000), Gerald Francis (1921–1994) and Henry James 'Harry' (1923–1943) (S5). So the open question is answered: the 'Anna Meier (Mrs. Frederick), 47', who died in Wilkes-Barre on 9 Feb 1940, was his wife Anna Mather (b. 28 Aug 1892) (S5).

Two months after Anna's death the 1940 census found Fred, 47 and widowed, lodging in Washington, DC, working 40 hours a week as a molder at the Navy Yard. He had been living in Wilkes-Barre in 1935 (S2). His youngest son Harry enlisted in Washington in 1942 and was killed in Italy in July 1943 as a staff sergeant in the Army Air Forces (see new person). Fred remarried by 1942 to Lucy Virginia (Puterbaugh) Bartleson, a widow 14 years older (1878–1959) (S5). He is placed at Dunellen, NJ in 1957. He died in lower Bucks County: the state index has 'MEIER FREDERICK A', 73, Bristol Twp., died 6 Mar 1966 (S4). The FS tree says 10 Mar 1966 at Trevose. He was buried at St. Mary's, Hanover Twp. (S5).
funFacts: He made castings for the U.S. Navy: in 1940 he was a molder at the Washington Navy Yard, the Navy's gun factory.
His 1917 draft card shows him following his father's trade as an iron moulder, at the Vulcan Iron Works in Wilkes-Barre.

conflicts.assessment: The state index reads 03/06/66 and Bristol Twp. (Bucks 09); FS gives 10 Mar at Trevose (also lower Bucks). The 10th may be the burial or obituary date. Prefer 6 Mar 1966 pending the certificate (file 022971).

confidenceRecommendation.justification: The WWI card gives his birth date (15 Sep 1892, Hazleton) and his parents' address (298 Barney St, the Henry J. Meier home in 1920). With the 1910 census showing him as Henry's son, the link rests on primary records.

openQuestionsResolved.question: Was his wife the Anna Meier (Mrs. Frederick) who died 9 Feb 1940 in Wilkes-Barre, aged 47?
openQuestionsResolved.answer: Yes, very probably: Anna Mather, b. 28 Aug 1892, d. 9 Feb 1940 Wilkes-Barre, married Fred 21 Apr 1915 (FS tree LRT7-WHC, with Find a Grave index at St. Mary's, Hanover Twp.). Fred was a widower in the April 1940 census.
